title: Apply for a Section 50 search (deceased estate)
summary: Learn how to apply for a Section 50 search to find out if a deceased person is recorded as a parent of any children.
intro:
If you're the executor, administrator or trustee of a deceased person's estate, and you need to find out if the deceased is recorded as being a parent of any children, you can apply for a Section 50 search. This search is often used to find beneficiaries of a deceased's estate.

You can visit a service centre and lodge your application in person, or post the information.
who_can_apply: The applicant must be the executor, administrator, or trustee of a deceased person's estate.
Searches are available for deceased females aged 12 to 60, and for males aged 12 until death.
If the deceased was born overseas, the search will only cover their time as a resident in NSW.
what_you_need: The details of the search required.
The completed PDF form: Apply for a Section 50 Search – PDF.

how_to_steps.text: Download and complete the Apply for a Section 50 Search – PDF.
Make sure you have all the required documentation.
Submit your application using the details on the form.

more_info.text: Certificates are sent by the Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages via registered post. They cannot be collected at a service centre.
Turnaround times commence when applications are received in full compliance with Registry requirements, and exclude delivery time.
If you change your mind, or decide the certificate is no longer required, your application fee will not be refunded.
Documents provided as proof of identity may have their authenticity verified through the online Certificate Validation Service (CertValid) and the National Document Verification Service (DVS).

faqs.q: Who can apply for a Section 50 search?
faqs.a: The executor, administrator, or trustee of a deceased person's estate can apply for this search.

faqs.q: What are the eligibility requirements for the deceased person?
faqs.a: Searches can be conducted for deceased females aged 12 to 60, and for males from age 12 until death. If the deceased was born overseas, only their time as a resident in NSW will be searched.

faqs.q: What documentation is required if I am the administrator or trustee?
faqs.a: If you are not a legal practitioner but are the administrator or trustee of the estate, you must provide 3 forms of your identification.
